source.title: Beyond Encoder Accumulation: Measuring Encoder Roles in Multi-Encoder VLMs
source.authors: Wei Ding; Yudong Zhang; Ruo-Bing Xie; Xing Sun; Jiansheng Chen; Yu Wang

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: It measures projector-representation CKA between retrained models with different amounts of encoder overlap. Similarity rises with overlap, and the authors interpret projector geometry as tied to encoder composition rather than only random initialization. This refines the convergence question but does not test model scaling or broad cross-architecture convergence.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the reported cross-model projector CKA results in Table 7. The paper's encoder benchmark scores, effective-rank results, pretrain-to-finetune drift CKA, and PID analyses do not measure convergence between models for the claim versions and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper is about encoder attribution in one multi-encoder VLM (Eagle-X5). It cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis only as motivation. Its only cross-model similarity result (Appendix A.6, Table 7) measures projector CKA between jointly trained Eagle-X5 models whose encoder subsets overlap. That tracks shared components inside one architecture, decoder, data and recipe, not convergence of independently trained models. It varies no scale, capability, seed or modality. There is no shared-0 bucket or seed-variance reference, and each subset is trained once, so it cannot separate a shared-ingredient explanation (V7) from anything else. It is a related construct, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but misplaced in emphasis. The main conclusions concern encoder roles in Eagle-X5. Retraining subsets (TR) ranks encoders differently from inference-time masking (IM). Capacity and Necessity are distinct axes. A ConvNeXt anchor plus a rank-expanding CLIP complement nearly matches the full pool. Pre-projector effective rank explains residual score variation. The CKA result is a supplementary diagnostic: the authors say pool composition, not random initialisation, drives projector geometry, but they never compare seeds.
record.recipe_differences: The paper measures projector CKA across retrained multi-encoder LVLM subsets; it does not reproduce the original scale-based convergence method or measure alignment between vision and language models.
record.method_sensitivity: Projector CKA similarity and its association with shared encoder count vary across task families; Knowledge has a notably weaker reported association.

fits_no_version.finding: Projector CKA between jointly trained Eagle-X5 models rises with the number of shared vision encoders (0.754 to 0.852 overall; rho=0.202), weaker for Knowledge (rho=0.086).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a fixed multi-encoder VLM recipe, representational similarity between models increases with the number of shared input components.

fits_no_version.finding: Within a jointly trained pool, pre-projector CKA between CLIP and other encoders ranges from about 0.65 (Pix2Struct) to 0.88 (EVA-02). A proxy PID decomposition finds the shared term dominant and synergy near zero (Table 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Heterogeneous vision encoders trained jointly behind a shared projector have largely overlapping representations as measured by CKA.

record.problems: The convergence-related CKA analysis is limited to one five-encoder Eagle-X5 pool with a Vicuna-7B decoder. The paper does not vary model scale or capability, compare different similarity metrics, or establish that the measured alignment is incomplete or plateaus. Each encoder subset was trained once; the authors describe small differences as directional rather than significance claims.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported Table 7 projector CKA values or correlations were left out. Other paper results were excluded because they do not measure the claim versions' convergence behavior.

untested.parts: No variation in model scale or capability; no independently trained models of different architectures, objectives or data.
No vision–language alignment on paired data.
Each subset is trained once, so no seed comparison. The 'not random initialisation' remark is untested.
Only CKA is used; no metric, setting or input-distribution comparison.
No test of plateau or incompleteness of independent-model alignment, nor of shared data or objectives as its cause.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T5/V7 'supports' label is not justified. Shared-encoder overlap is shared model components within one recipe, not shared data or objectives across independently trained models. No zero-overlap or seed baseline exists. Single training run per subset; preprint.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability, and no comparison of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
No comparison of vision and language representations for paired images and captions, or of their alignment as model quality changes.
Models are retrained across encoder subsets, not compared across random initializations of the same architecture to test shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No test for recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
The paper reports CKA results across encoder-overlap groups, but does not compare similarity metrics, metric settings, or input distributions to test metric or data dependence.

The study tests whether projector similarity varies with shared encoder count in one Eagle-X5 pool. It does not establish that alignment is far from complete or plateaus, nor distinguish shared training data or objectives from a common model of reality across a broad range of architectures and training setups.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Eagle-X5 retrained model pairs, overall and grouped by task family
reader_labels.reason: Projector CKA rises across the reported shared-encoder-count buckets overall (0.754 to 0.852), and the overall association with overlap is positive (ρ=0.202, p below 0.001), consistent with shared encoder composition contributing to similarity; see T7-overall-s1 through T7-overall-s4 and T7-rho-overall.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across the four task families and the single Eagle-X5 encoder pool
reader_labels.reason: The association varies by family, including a weaker Knowledge correlation (ρ=0.086), and the experiment does not test scale, generalization beyond this pool, or whether similarity is incomplete or plateaus; see T7-rho-general through T7-rho-vision and the family CKA rows.
